subject: Model fit evaluation — follow-up & next steps
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-15T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model fit evaluation — follow-up & next steps

Thanks again for the call earlier today, Samir — really helpful to see the PayGrid flows. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

1) What we heard
- Primary goal: migrate invoice classification and intent routing off your proprietary baseline to reduce cost while maintaining >=95% parity on intent accuracy and <=2% drop on end-to-end routing accuracy.
- Data access: you can provide a 5k-sample anonymized set (prefer row-level labels + one example per class).
- Constraints: <150ms p95 latency target for short prompts, and strict PII handling (no customer text stored in hosted evals).

2) Redwood recommended starting models (open candidates)
- Llama2-13B-Chat-q4: best line-item balance of quality & latency when quantized.
- Mistral-Instruct-13B: strong instruction-following for routing edge cases.
- Falcon-40B-instruct-lite (trimmed prompt sets): for high-complexity parsing if we need a larger baseline.

3) Parity & acceptance thresholds (suggested)
- Intent classification macro-accuracy >=95% vs your baseline on the 5k eval set.
- End-to-end routing degradation <=2% absolute.
- No regression in high-severity intents (top-10 revenue impacting intents) — per-intent recall delta <=3%.

4) Proposed evaluation plan (deliverables)
- Redwood runs a 2-week sandbox eval using the sample dataset + your prompt set.
- Deliverables: benchmark-summary-20260816.pdf (high-level metrics), paygrid_prompt_set_v1.csv (prompts we used), and a parity report with confusion matrices.
- Quick decision gates after week 1: if macro-accuracy <92% we iterate on prompt engineering and model selection.

5) Next steps / asks from PayGrid
- Share anonymized 5k sample with labels and a short list of high-severity intents (CSV preferred).
- Confirm if we can run the eval on Redwood Hosted with a strict no-storage flag (we will show ephemeral-only logs).
- 30-min sync next Tue (8/18) to review initial runs.

I’ve attached the eval plan and the initial prompt set we discussed. Marissa & Aditya — looping you in for any technical constraints we should enforce during the sandbox (quantization settings, batching targets).

Best,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0123

Attachments: paygrid_prompt_set_v1.csv, redwood_eval_plan.pdf

From: Samir Patel <samir@paygrid.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-15T17:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model fit evaluation — follow-up & next steps

Thanks Lauren — appreciate the clear summary. A couple quick clarifications before we send data over: 

- Baseline: our internal model is tuned on 50k historical conversations. For parity comparisons, should we compare against your tuned runs on our 5k sample or against metrics from our full 50k baseline? We’d prefer the latter if possible.
- Latency: the <150ms p95 is a strict customer SLO for some routes — can you confirm expected p95 when running Llama2-13B-Chat-q4 quantized on your hosted instance?
- Cost: what’s the order-of-magnitude delta we should expect (tokens / run) between the open candidates and the proprietary baseline? High-level is fine.

Also, we cannot share raw customer IDs in the sample. We will provide the anonymized CSV with labels and a note on high-severity intents by EOD Monday.

—Samir
Samir Patel
Head of ML Ops | PayGrid
samir@paygrid.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-16T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model fit evaluation — follow-up & next steps

Hi Samir — great questions, answered inline below.

- Baseline comparison: we can do both, but for an apples-to-apples parity read you’ll get two reports — (A) tuned-on-5k vs your baseline-on-50k (est. delta due to sample size noted) and (B) tuned-on-5k vs tuned-open-model runs. The parity thresholds I listed are relative to your full baseline metrics unless you prefer otherwise.

- Latency: for Llama2-13B-Chat-q4 quantized on Redwood Hosted (bfloat16 or Q4_0 depending on kernel), typical p95 for short prompts (<=256 tokens) is 90–140ms in our tests. We’ll benchmark on your exact prompt set during the sandbox and include per-route p95. If you need a hard SLA at 150ms we can prioritize lower-latency kernel selection and stricter batching profiles.

- Cost: ballpark — open 13B models (quantized) typically run at ~30–50% of the per-token cost of a large proprietary 70B baseline, depending on request shape and KV cache reuse. We’ll include a token-level cost breakdown in the benchmark summary.

We’ll proceed once you send the anonymized CSV and confirm the sandbox execution mode (hosted ephemeral/no-storage). I’ve attached an initial benchmark summary with sample numbers from a similar customer so you can set expectations.

Marissa / Aditya — please note Samir asked for the strict p95 numbers and a cost delta estimate; can we prepare a short appendix in the parity report that shows per-model p95 and per-token cost assumptions? Also include quantization profile we recommend (Q4_0 vs Q4_K_M) and a note on accuracy regressions we typically see when moving from baseline to quantized open models.

Thanks — I’ll tentatively schedule Tue 8/18 10:00 AM PT for a 30-min sync; let me know if that works.

Best,
Lauren

Attachments: benchmark-summary-20260816.pdf

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-08-16T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Model fit evaluation — internal notes on parity thresholds

Marissa / Aditya — forwarding the thread and calling out the internal action items so we don’t miss anything: 

1) Parity appendix: please produce a 1-page appendix that maps our metrics to PayGrid’s baseline metrics (they provided aggregate numbers — we must estimate sample-size adjustments). Include: macro-accuracy, per-intent recall, confusion matrix for top-10 intents.

2) Latency matrix: run quick perf tests for Llama2-13B-Chat-q4 (Q4_0) and Mistral-Instruct-13B (Q4_K_M) with the following shapes: short prompts (<=128 tokens), medium (128-512), and long (512-1k). Return p50/p95/p99 numbers and a rough cost-per-1k-requests estimate.

3) Regression guardrails: draft language we can use in the parity report that sets acceptance thresholds (intent macro-accuracy >=95%, end-to-end <=2% drop) and outlines remediation steps (prompt tuning, small-shot fine-tune, fallback to dedicated baseline instance).

Timeline: can you have drafts of the appendix + latency matrix by EOD Mon (8/17)? I’ll incorporate into the parity report we send to Samir on Tue before the sync.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate scheduling.

Lauren
